date: 21 Feb 1437/8 (Florentine style), with copies of letters of Oct 1437
title: Puccio Pucci to Cosimo de' Medici at Ferrara, Florence, 21 Feb 1437/8, with copies of Neri di Gino Capponi's letters of Oct 1437: cipher words and code numbers throughout a clear text, bare (MAP XLIV doc. 21)
correspondents: Puccio d'Antonio Pucci -> Cosimo de' Medici (enclosing copies of Neri di Gino Capponi -> Puccio Pucci)
place: Florence (copies from the Florentine camp in Lombardy, 1437)
language: Italian (nomenclator: cipher words in invented letter-signs plus code numbers)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza XLIV, doc. 21 (c. 21r-v)
folio_note: Image positions 43 (c. 21r) and 44 (c. 21v), viewer id 56470. Recto: heading 'Copie di piu lettere copiate ...', then two copied letters signed 'Neri di Gino Capponi' to 'Puccio d'Antonio di Puccio' dated Oct 1437, then a third copied passage; verso: letter signed 'Puccio', 'In Firenze a di xxi di febraio 1437', addressed to Cosimo. About 20 cipher groups of 2-9 signs each, set off by triple-dot separators, plus code numbers (40, 42, 43, 78) standing for names.
status: Bare on the images viewed 13 Nov 2026: no interlinear, marginal or foot decipherment on recto or verso. The cipher groups are words inside a clear text (a partly enciphered letter), not whole lines. Not found in DECODE, Tomokiyo or Ross.
why: Medici partisans' secret reports to Cosimo during his Ferrara embassy of 1438 and Neri Capponi's letters from the Lombard war of 1437; among the earliest Medici cipher letters in the MAP and from the Medici regime's first years.
score_note: Scored from the images viewed in the b174 backfill pass, 13 Nov 2026: about 20 short cipher words with clear context around each and recurring code numbers; context is rich but the cipher sample is small.
verify: Transcribe all cipher groups on c. 21r-v at 1272 px; compare the sign set with the Florentine keys of 1414-1440 printed by Meister (1902) pp. 42-50 and the 1425 Urbino cipher (DECODE R3754-R3757); look for other Puccio or Averardo letters in MAP XLIV, XII and XIII with the same signs.
source: ASF Mediceo avanti il Principato images (MAP filza XLIV paging), b174 backfill, Nov 2026
prior_art: open as far as checked (13 Nov 2026): DECODE 'Puccio' and 'Capponi' 0 records, no Florentine 1437/1438 record; Tomokiyo italian.htm lists no 1430s Medici letter; Ross 1910 prints no Puccio letter.

seen.where: ASF MAP filza XLIV pos 43 and 44 via IIIF at 1272 px (https://archiviodistatofirenze.cultura.gov.it/iipsrv/iipsrv.fcgi?IIIF=/data/iip-data/asfi/mediceo_avanti_principato/00100044/A0000043.ptif), recto read in two native halves and verso at 600 px, 13 Nov 2026
seen.extent: One leaf: recto about 45 lines (copies of two or three letters), verso about 25 lines (Puccio's covering letter); about 20 cipher groups across both sides plus code numbers
seen.cipher: Cipher words written in invented letter-like signs (forms resembling Greek capitals, inverted V, L, X, Z, H) with ':.' triple-dot separators, mixed with code numbers 40, 42, 43, 78 standing for persons, inside clear Italian text. Nothing written above, below or beside the cipher groups.

prior_art.decode: de-crypt.org/decrypt-web/RecordsList: search=Puccio 'No records found', search=Capponi 'No records found', search=1437 and 1438 return only ACA Barcelona 1437 and BAV Urb. lat. 998 items, search=Cosimo lists ASFi Cifrari vol. 3 keys of 1570s (13 Nov 2026). Nothing from MAP XLIV.
prior_art.tomokiyo: cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/italian.htm (50,193 bytes, 13 Nov 2026), Florence section: Meister 1902 pp. 42-50 (Florentine keys from 1414), Bourdeau's 1425 Urbino report (DECODE R3754-R3757), Lasry's Acciaiuoli 1478, Vito 2025, Guicciardini 1590s; no Pucci, Capponi or Ferrara 1438 letter.
prior_art.lasry: Repo docs/lasry/ folders (berny1607 ... vulcob1573, 56 names) include no 15th-c. Florentine item other than the Acciaiuoli 1478 solution named by Tomokiyo; web search for Lasry with Medici 1430s cipher found nothing on MAP XLIV.
prior_art.edition: No edition of incoming letters to Cosimo covers filza XLIV. Ross, Lives of the Early Medici (1910, Gutenberg 74973, full text grepped 13 Nov 2026) translates 1438 letters from Sforza and the Dieci but none from Puccio or Neri Capponi; its only cipher mention is Sforza's 'your letter in cipher'.
prior_art.literature: Web searches on Puccio Pucci, Neri di Gino Capponi, Cosimo at Ferrara 1438 and MAP XLIV found Kent-style political histories and Ross, no transcription or decipherment of doc. 21. Vito, HistoCrypt 2025 (Florentine polyalphabetic key) could not be opened: the dspace.ut.ee PDF reset the connection and was not retried.
